title: Micro-Influencer Marketing: Follower Counts, Programs, and Real Campaign Examples
summary: Learn what counts as a micro-influencer, how follower counts compare to macro-influencers, and how to build a micro-influencer program with real examples, pricing, and measurement.
body_markdown:
## Micro vs Macro Influencers: Followers, Cost, and Real ROI Economics


### Head-to-Head: Reach, Engagement Rate, Cost per Post, and Conversion


A macro influencer generally reaches a larger audience in one placement; a micro creator can offer a more concentrated community and let you spread spend across several voices. Influencer Marketing Hub places macro accounts around 100,000 to 1 million followers. Demand Curve reports that micro-influencer posts can cost under $500, while celebrity-level posts can exceed $50,000. Actual rates depend on platform, deliverables, usage rights, exclusivity, and creator demand.


Compare proposals by estimated engaged audience and campaign objective, not just fee or follower total. A view, click, or sale is a different outcome, so define the conversion you want before comparing offers.


### The Engagement Curve: Why Rates Fall as Follower Counts Rise


Smaller creators often have a closer relationship with a focused audience, while larger accounts reach more people with varied interests.


These are reported patterns, not guarantees for an individual account. Check recent posts and calculate engagement consistently with a defined denominator, such as interactions divided by followers.


### The Worked Math: A 12K Creator at 4.5% vs a 90K Creator at 0.8%


Estimate potential engagement to compare creators. The larger account produces more estimated interactions in this example, but may also charge a higher fee and reach a different audience.


Calculate cost per engagement by dividing the post fee by estimated interactions. These illustrative inputs are not market-rate claims; use verified account data and actual quotes.


### When to Choose Macro (and When Micro Wins)


Choose macro for broad awareness, a large one-time audience, or a concept built around a creator’s public profile. Choose micro creators for niche relevance, multiple audience segments, testing creative approaches, or building repeat partnerships. A micro[influencer marketing strategy](https://www.reacherapp.com/blog/influencer-marketing-strategy-a-step-by-step-guide-with-real-examples) can combine tiers, giving each creator a distinct role rather than expecting one account to deliver every outcome.


Compare total campaign cost, expected reach, engagement quality, audience fit, and the conversion event you can track. Test a small, clearly defined group, then scale the creator mix that meets your goals.
